h: Foxes, Tigers and a putter at the ready
p: Leicester is a proper sporting city. Leicester City pulled off one of football's greatest shocks by winning the Premier League in 2016, and the Leicester Tigers are one of English rugby's best-known clubs, playing at Welford Road. So a round of adventure golf here can get competitive quickly. Consider yourselves warned.

For practical planning, allow roughly an hour for your round. Bigger groups may take a little longer, so give yourself some breathing room if you've got food or a film booked afterwards. Get there a few minutes early, choose your scorekeeper wisely, and if there's a toddler in the group, let them go first on each hole and enjoy the chaos.

Beyond the sights already mentioned, Leicester has a few gems worth adding to your day. Abbey Park, just north of the centre, has a lake, gardens and the ruins of Leicester Abbey, where Cardinal Wolsey died. Curve, the striking theatre in the Cultural Quarter, hosts big touring shows and musicals. The Leicester Museum and Art Gallery on New Walk is another good choice for a rainy hour.

With a car, Bradgate Park is a short drive out and a real favourite with locals. It's a big expanse of open parkland with wild deer and the ruins of the house where Lady Jane Grey was born. Mix that with a round of golf and a curry in the evening, and you've nailed a Leicester day.
